newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes higher as soybeans surge.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes higher as soybeans surge.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on a rally in soybeans tied to concerns about cool weather moving into the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
"The colder weather and crop deterioration (soybeans) provided us strength all day. It was surprisingly strong for a pre-report day," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Cool weather would slow development of the corn crop but would be more detrimental to soybeans than corn, traders said.
USDA Monday said the U.S. corn crop was 11 percent mature as of Sunday, behind 23 percent average maturity for that time of year.
An average of analysts' estimates put the U.S. corn crop at 8.857 billion bushels, above USDA's outlook in August for 8.695 billion.
Gains were limited by weak cash basis markets, increased corn harvesting and hedge selling, the traders said.
Corn futures closed one to 4-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with September up 3-1/2 at $3.65-3/4 a bushel. December was 3-1/2 higher at $3.34-1/4.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 45,000, up from 34,436 Monday.
Aggressive trading was noted in corn options.

FIMAT Futures bought 2,000 March $3.80 calls at 8-3/4 to 9-1/4 cents, Term Commodities bought 700 December $4.20 calls at 1-3/8 to 1-1/2, Smith Barney bought 1,500 March $3.80 calls and Griffin Trading sold 1,800 December $3.40 calls at 12-1/2 to 13-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 19,000, up from 12,298 Monday.
